subject: Assessment: model fit for SafeHarbor claims — actionable recs + rollback path
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@safeharborins.com>, Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@safeharborins.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Assessment: model fit for SafeHarbor claims — first-pass recs and artifacts

Hi Sara / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the immediate items I promised to send over:

Summary of findings (post-demo / quick eval):
- Safety/claim hallucination risk: we saw a small increase (~2.8% false-claim assertions) on a 1k-sample of your claims dataset when comparing Redwood v1.4.2 -> v1.5.0.
- Latency: v1.5.0 reduces median latency by ~11% at 512 tokens, but some prompt patterns degrade QA precision.
- Prompt sensitivity: a handful of template prompts in your prompt_set_claims_review.txt show divergent completions (examples inside benchmarks_safeharbor.csv).

Attachments I uploaded (zipped evals + prompts):
- safeharbor_eval_pack_v1.zip (eval harness, sample traces)
- benchmarks_safeharbor.csv (diffed examples & token-level deltas)
- prompt_set_claims_review.txt (your annotated prompts + suggested rewrites)

Recommended immediate options (tradeoffs included):
1) Emergency pin to v1.4.2-quant (conservative): eliminates the observed regression; no behavioral changes expected.
2) Serve v1.5.0 behind a quality gate for the affected routes (canary 10% traffic + eval hooks) — faster, requires 48–72h of monitoring.
3) Quick prompt adjustments (low effort): we can apply 3 prompt rewrites that reduce hallucination rate by ~1.5% with no infra change.

Next steps I suggest:
- Please confirm whether you want us to initiate an emergency pin (option #1) or run a regulated canary (option #2).
- If pin, we’ll schedule a 30-min window for the change and provide rollback notes.

Links: full eval pack -> https://drive.redwood.com/drive/safeharbor/eval-pack-v1

Thanks — I’ll await confirmation.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@safeharborins.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Assessment: model fit for SafeHarbor claims — first-pass recs and artifacts

Thanks Evelyn — appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A couple of clarifying Qs before we pick a path: 

- The increase in false-claim assertions: is that concentrated on medical-exclusion language, or is it broad? We’ve got a small but material compliance bar here.
- If we pin to v1.4.2, what happens to ongoing throughput? Does the pin bump our cost/affect our reserved capacity?
- We noticed two live incidents in our dev env where v1.5.0 marked claims as “fraudulent” where earlier versions did not. We need a fast option.

If pinning is the fastest mitigation, please proceed — but we need a short note to our procurement team (procure@safeharborins.com) saying this is a functional rollback and that SLA economics are unchanged.

—Sara
Head of Claims Automation
SafeHarbor Insurance
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@safeharborins.com>, Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@safeharborins.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Assessment: model fit for SafeHarbor claims — first-pass recs and artifacts

Sara —

Short answers:
- The regression is concentrated in medical-exclusion language + long nested conditionals (see benchmarks row 42–79). It’s not uniform across all claim types.
- Pinning to v1.4.2 is purely a serving-level change (we’ll update your route to reference the older model hash). It does not change your reserved capacity; costs are the same.

If you sign off, proposed plan to execute immediately:
1) Emergency pin to v1.4.2-quant for the "claims-extract" route (scheduled in a 30-minute window).
2) Run a post-pin smoke test (50 gold samples from your eval pack).
3) Parallel: we’ll run a 10% canary of v1.5.0 on a non-critical route to collect additional diffs and iterate prompt rewrites.

I’ve pasted the minimal API steps below for transparency — happy to run the change if you authorize.

-- API pin example (conceptual) --
POST /admin/routes/claims-extract/pin
Body: { model_version: "v1.4.2-quant", reason: "regression observed on v1.5.0 - approval from SafeHarbor" }
Response: 200 -> route model pinned, previous_version archived

Please reply with: "Approve pin to v1.4.2-quant" or "Run canary". If we get no reply in 2 hours we’ll hold.

Regards,
Evelyn
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Quick note from the commercial side: pinning is fine operationally, but procurement will want the note Sara mentioned (procure@safeharborins.com). If we’re taking a canary approach, can we also confirm a rollback SLA (i.e., Redwood will revert within X hours if canary metrics cross thresholds)? Monica — can you own the monitoring thresholds?

Short reply OK from me: "Approve pin to v1.4.2-quant" — pending procurement note.

Karthik

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Plan confirmed: emergency pin + validation checklist

Thanks all — Per Sara's ask and Karthik's note, we’ll execute option #1 (emergency pin to v1.4.2-quant) in the next available 30-min window. Procurement note included below for the archive.

Procurement notification (for SafeHarbor):
- Action: functional rollback of model for route "claims-extract" to v1.4.2-quant.
- Reason: observed quality regression with v1.5.0 on medical-exclusion language; mitigation required to preserve compliance behavior.
- Impact to economics: no change to committed reserved capacity or pricing; this is a serving configuration change only.
- Contact: procurement questions -> procure@redwood.ai / accounts@redwood.ai

Execution checklist (what we will do now):
- T+0: pin route to v1.4.2-quant.
- T+5m: run 50-gold-sample smoke tests from safeharbor_eval_pack_v1.zip; expect <1% mismatch vs baseline.
- T+15m: monitor for anomalous error spikes and latency regressions.
- T+24h: provide a results summary and sample diffs (CSV) and an action recommendation (continue pinned vs graduated canary).

If anyone needs us to delay, reply within 20 minutes. Otherwise we’ll proceed and publish the runbook to your Drive folder.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
